## Summary

The actual prompt text behind the **/retro** skill announced at AI Engineer Paris — first time the mechanics are visible without watching the talk. The prompt, verbatim:

> /retro take a look at as many GitHub PR review comments as you have access to from my team. Create suggestions for updates to CODING_STANDARDS.md (breaking into multiple files as needed).
>
> Makes your PR comments inform the code going forward.

Mechanics revealed: **input** = the team's real GitHub PR review history ("as many as you have access to"); **output** = *suggestions* for CODING_STANDARDS.md updates, not auto-writes; **structure** = the standards file may be split into multiple files as the corpus grows; **effect** = review comments stop being one-off corrections and become training data for future code.

## Why it matters

- **Answers half of the pending /retro inbox task** (watch the talk, extract what triggers it / what it writes / where findings land). Now known: what it writes (suggestions for CODING_STANDARDS.md, possibly split), where findings land (the standards files), what triggers it (a named, manually-invoked prompt). Still missing: how suggestions get accepted/rejected, and whether there's dedup against existing rules.
- **"Suggestions" = draft-and-show**, the same governance posture this company runs on — a model pass proposes the standards diff, a human reviews it. The mining is automated; the merge is not.
- **The multi-file split directly addresses the growth concern** flagged in [[2026-09-26-pocock-coding-standards-accretion]] (an accreting file becoming a context sink). Notably Pocock's answer is *structural* (split into files) rather than *subtractive* (prune) — the accretion/deletion tension with [[2026-09-26-drummatick-openclaw-test-audit]] stays open.
- **The loop is now fully specified across the vault cluster**: reviewable PRs produce comments ([[2026-09-06-pocock-reviewable-ai-prs]]) → /retro mines comments into standards → standards accrete ("only empty for 5 minutes", [[2026-09-26-pocock-coding-standards-accretion]]) → a cheap model enforces them ([[2026-09-26-pocock-jev-fuzzy-linter]], [[2026-10-01-pocock-fix-one-thing-skill]]) → /pr raises review quality back into the loop ([[2026-10-01-pocock-retro-pr-announcement]]).
- **Our own mirror**: this company's skills Pitfalls sections are exactly this loop run by hand. The tweet argues for automating the mining step over real review history — a candidate for our own end-of-task checklist (the decision the pending task defers).
- **Skepticism gates**: it's a "prompt of the day" share, not a released tool — whether the named /retro *skill* does more than this single prompt (scoping, dedup, caching) is unverified until the talk. "As many PR review comments as you have access to" implies context limits bite fast on a large team; the multi-file split reads as the workaround, not a nicety.
